newsitem.title: USA: Texas grand jury probes Marine border shooting.
newsitem.headline: Texas grand jury probes Marine border shooting.

text.p: A Texas grand jury met on Wednesday to examine whether U.S. Marines who shot dead a teenager as he herded goats near the Mexican border were acting in self-defence or killed him in cold blood.

The death of 18-year-old Esequiel Hernandez on May 20 in the Texas border town of Redford has sparked a dispute over the use of military forces in the border war on drugs and demands that the Marine who fired the fatal shot be tried for murder.
District Attorney Albert Valadez said the grand jury was given audio and video evidence, photographs and laboratory results.

He said the grand jury will not reconvene until Aug. 14 because he wants to subpoena eight more federal witnesses but has not yet served them because federal authorities have not been cooperative. He declined to give details.

Relatives and friends of Hernandez want Marine Corp. Clemente Banuelos convicted of murder for shooting Hernandez and are also calling for measures against his superiors in the Task Force Six military unit that helps border law enforcement agencies in the war on drugs.

"The fact that he is dead is not only the responsibility of the Marines but the people who put them there," said Melvin LaFollette, a member of the Redford Citizens' Committee for Justice that was set up after the shooting.
But Banuelos' attorney, Jack Zimmermann, said his client opened fire after Hernandez took a shot at another Marine.
"He shot in defence of one of his fellow teammates. That is what he was supposed to do and that's not a crime in Texas," Zimmerman said.
Hernandez' family insists he was herding goats at the time and only carried his .22-calibre rifle to scare away wild dogs. They claim he was shot dead in cold blood.
The use of Task Force Six units was suspended along the U.S.-Mexico border after the shooting.
